data: For fiscal 2025, Apple reported research and development expense of $34,550 million (about $34.6 billion) for the year ended September 27, 2025, while Microsoft reported $32,488 million (about $32.5 billion) for the year ended June 30, 2025. Apple's figure is about 1.06 times Microsoft's, a gap of roughly $2.1 billion or 6.3%. The two fiscal years end three months apart, so the periods do not line up exactly. Relative to revenue the order flips: Microsoft's R&D was about 11.5% of its $281,724 million in revenue, compared with about 8.3% of Apple's $416,161 million in net sales. Both companies increased R&D from fiscal 2024, Microsoft from $29,510 million (up 10.1%) and Apple from $31,370 million (up 10.1%).
